# rag-ferrite — Hybrid RAG engine (Rust) — binary: `ragfer`

> Personal RAG engine — simple, fast, Rust. Single binary `ragfer` (15 MB), one DB, native collections. MCP-native + integrated CLI + TUI monitor.

## What it does

Turns documents (PDF, DOCX, TXT, MD, HTML) into queryable knowledge with semantic understanding.
Single Rust binary, SQLite storage, multi-collection, hybrid search with LLM-powered intelligence.

## Source structure

```
src/
├── main.rs (359 lines) — entry point, CLI dispatch, server startup
├── server.rs (191 lines) — RagFerriteServer struct + MCP tool methods
├── client.rs (384 lines) — CLI client (subcommands via ureq HTTP)
├── config.rs (884 lines) — TOML config loading
├── llm.rs (802 lines) — LLM provider, context generation, response parsing
├── chunker.rs (837 lines) — text chunking (recursive + parent-child)
├── ingestion.rs (680 lines) — ingestion queue + progress
├── pipeline.rs (470 lines) — query pipeline, classification, cache
├── api.rs (392 lines) — HTTP routes (axum)
├── service.rs (378 lines) — shared business logic (MCP + HTTP)
├── reranker.rs (330 lines) — reranker (LLM, Cohere, Disabled)
├── embedding.rs (246 lines) — embedding provider
├── types.rs (228 lines) — shared types
├── params.rs (141 lines) — parameter structs (IngestConfig, QueryParams, etc.)
├── extractor.rs (119 lines) — PDF/DOCX/text extraction
├── tag_rules.rs (181 lines) — tag rules + sanitize + global state
├── monitor/
│   ├── mod.rs (630 lines) — App struct, event loop, key handling
│   ├── ui.rs (947 lines) — ratatui rendering
│   └── api.rs (128 lines) — HTTP fetch for monitor
├── engine/
│   ├── mod.rs (221 lines) — DB init, schema migrations, stats
│   ├── ingest.rs (829 lines) — core ingestion
│   ├── search.rs (137 lines) — hybrid search
│   ├── query.rs (199 lines) — query helpers
│   ├── benchmark.rs (225 lines) — benchmarks
│   ├── indexes.rs (129 lines) — sqlite-vec/FTS5 index management
│   ├── heat.rs (348 lines) — collection heat tracking
│   ├── tag_routing.rs (163 lines) — tag-based routing
│   ├── tags.rs (129 lines) — tag DB operations
│   ├── precheck.rs (145 lines) — pre-ingestion check
│   ├── chunk_heat.rs (109 lines) — chunk heat tracking
│   ├── activity_log.rs (68 lines) — activity log ring buffer
│   ├── chunk_counter.rs (22 lines) — atomic chunk counter
│   └── cancel.rs (20 lines) — cancel flag
```

No `bin/` directory. No standalone `rag-monitor`. Monitor is `src/monitor/`.

## Ingestion pipeline

```
Document → Extract text (pdftotext / docx-lite / raw)
         → Chunk (auto/recursive/parent-child, configurable)
         → Relevance scoring (LLM rates 1-10, filters junk)
         → Contextual retrieval (LLM adds context prefix to each chunk)
         → Auto-tagging (LLM generates 2-3 tags per chunk)
         → Embed batch → Store in SQLite + sqlite-vec index + FTS5/BM25

Parent-child ingestion commits each parent group atomically with its children and their FTS5/sqlite-vec rows. Parent and child rows use the canonical `chunk_role` values (`parent`/`child`), and parents carry a stable `logical_parent_index` so interrupted work resumes from the exact committed set. Content deduplication uses SHA-256; legacy hashes are upgraded lazily when matched.

REST and MCP ingestion share one bounded mpsc worker queue. Queue-full requests return `error_code: queue_full`; inline content is capped by `advanced.max_inline_content_bytes`, HTTP bodies by `advanced.http_body_limit_bytes`, and jobs by `advanced.ingestion_timeout_secs`. Local path tools canonicalize requests and enforce `advanced.allowed_ingest_roots`, including symlink escapes. Rebuild and flush operations run through the same worker, so index updates are serialized with ingestion and progress covers every transport. Long synchronous SQLite searches and status/list reads are dispatched to Tokio's blocking pool; SQLite remains WAL-enabled with one serialized shared connection, and the unused `db_pool_size` setting was removed.

Filtered vector and BM25 searches resolve one shared allowed chunk-ID set per hybrid query. sqlite-vec and FTS5 use adaptive over-fetching so matches outside the initial candidate window are not lost; brute-force vector search applies SQL filters directly. The query cache key includes every search filter, canonicalizes unordered ID lists, and carries a global data version incremented after source, chunk, deletion, and collection mutations.
```

Engine uses `params::IngestConfig` (not IngestOptions — deleted). Constructed from `Config` in `main.rs`, passed to engine methods.

### What gets filtered at ingestion

- Tables of contents, index pages, boilerplate
- Chunks scoring below `min_relevance_score` (default: 5/10)
- Duplicates detected via content hashing
- Chunks too small to be meaningful (< 200 chars merged with previous)

### Ingestion quality check

Before ingesting, use `check_ingestion()` to preview:
- Character count, estimated chunk count
- Language detection
- Duplicate detection against existing documents
- Warnings for very large or very small documents

## CI quality gates

GitHub Actions runs formatting, Clippy with `-D warnings`, all-target tests, and `cargo audit` on pull requests and `main`. The repository uses a documented compatibility allowlist for the existing lint baseline; new warnings outside that list fail CI. Cargo dependencies and build artifacts are cached, and Dependabot checks Cargo dependencies weekly.

REST and MCP adapters share structured application errors with `error_code` values. HTTP maps validation to 400, auth to 401/403, missing resources to 404, conflicts to 409, queue backpressure to 429, and internal failures to 500.

HTTP binds to loopback by default. Non-loopback binding requires configured API authentication unless `advanced.unsafe_bind_without_auth` is explicitly enabled. MCP Host-header allowlisting is configured with `advanced.allowed_hosts` and is separate from authentication. One middleware protects both REST and `/mcp`; credentials are re-read from the active `.env` state so key rotation takes effect immediately, with atomic replacement and restrictive permissions.

## Query pipeline

```
Query → Classify (simple / standard / complex)
      → [standard/complex] Query expansion (LLM multi-query)
      → Hybrid retrieval (BM25 + sqlite-vec + FTS5 + RRF fusion)
      → [standard/complex] LLM reranking (0-1 scoring of top results)
      → Query cache (TTL 300s in memory)
      → Quality gate (confidence score)
      → [low confidence] Corrective RAG (reformulate + retry)
      → Return top-k chunks with tags and scores
```

## MCP Tools (16)

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `query_documents(query, collection?, limit?)` | Hybrid search with filters, reranking, expansion, cache |
| `ingest_file(file_path, collection?)` | Ingest PDF, DOCX, TXT, MD |
| `ingest_data(content, source, collection?, format?)` | Ingest raw text, HTML, or markdown |
| `delete_file(source)` | Remove document and all its chunks |
| `list_files()` | List indexed documents |
| `status()` | Engine status and document count |
| `read_chunk_neighbors(source_id, chunk_index)` | Expand context around a chunk |
| `check_ingestion(file_path?, content?, source_name?)` | Preview document quality before ingestion |
| `benchmark(file_path, collection?, limit?)` | Evaluate versioned golden-dataset retrieval metrics: Recall@k, precision, MRR, nDCG, empty-result rate, and latency percentiles |
| `collection_heat()` | Collection heat tracking |
| `chunk_qa()` | Chunk-level QA: dead/cold chunks grouped by source |
| `suggest_collection(query)` | Tag routing: suggest best collection for a query |
| `tag_map()` | Full tag → collection mapping with chunk counts |
| `reassign_collection(source_id, collection)` | Move a source and its chunks to a different collection |
| `rebuild_indexes()` | Rebuild FTS5 and checkpoint SQLite |
| `flush_indexes()` | Flush SQLite/WAL state and refresh derived indexes |

### Retrieval evaluation

The `benchmark` MCP tool accepts either the legacy JSON array of golden entries or a versioned object:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "entries": [
    {"question": "...", "relevant_source_ids": [1, 2], "expected_keywords": []}
  ]
}
```

It reports Recall@k, precision@k, MRR, nDCG, empty-result rate, p50/p95 latency, and per-query details. It evaluates retrieval only; answer-level faithfulness is outside the server's scope. Semantic chunking remains optional and disabled; the reproducible evaluation protocol is in `docs/semantic-chunking-evaluation.md`. Persistent per-operation LLM caching is deferred until operation-level telemetry demonstrates meaningful repeated cost; see `docs/llm-cache-evaluation.md`. The optional web library console is enabled with `advanced.web_ui_enabled = true` and served at `/`. It uses authenticated REST for text ingestion, progress, source listing/deletion, and retrieval inspection; it remains MCP-first and does not host a chatbot or model. Indexed metadata is rendered through DOM text nodes, never HTML interpolation. See `docs/web-interface-plan.md`.

## HTTP API Endpoints

| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/status` | Engine status, version, document count |
| POST | `/api/ingest` | Unified ingest — `file_path` (single) or `paths` (batch), `move_after_ingest` |
| POST | `/api/ingest/data` | Ingest raw text content |
| GET | `/api/ingest/progress` | Batch progress: files, chunks, live elapsed/speed/ETA, activity log, errors, per-file results |
| POST | `/api/query` | Hybrid search with reranking |
| GET | `/api/documents` | List all sources |
| GET | `/api/documents/{id}` | Get document details |
| DELETE | `/api/documents/{id}` | Delete document |
| GET | `/api/graph` | Source relationship graph |
| POST | `/api/flush-indexes` | Refresh derived indexes + WAL checkpoint |
| POST | `/api/rebuild-indexes` | Full index rebuild |
| POST | `/api/service/cancel-batch` | Cancel running batch |
| POST | `/api/service/stop` | Graceful server shutdown |

## CLI (`ragfer`)

- `ragfer` (no args) → TUI monitor (default)
- `ragfer serve` / `-d` → daemon (MCP + HTTP)
- Client subcommands: `status`, `list`, `query`, `progress`, `ingest-file`, `ingest-batch`, `ingest-data`, `delete`, `flush`, `rebuild`, `cancel`, `stop`, `update`, `setup`, `monitor`

All client commands hit the HTTP API. Server must be running.

Client config: `~/.config/ragfer/config.toml` (url key) + `~/.config/ragfer/.env` (RAG_API_KEY).

## Collections

Multi-collection in the same SQLite database. Each MCP tool accepts an optional `collection` parameter.
Collections are created on-the-fly — no setup needed.

### Tag routing

The `collection_tags` table maps each tag to the collections where it appears, with chunk counts. Auto-populated during ingestion. Heat tracking columns on `chunks` table: `query_count` (incremented on query hit) and `last_queried_at` (timestamp). Chunk heat updates use an async batched pattern (mpsc channel + 30s flush) to avoid blocking queries.

## Config

Server config: `config.toml` alongside the binary. Client config: `~/.config/ragfer/config.toml`.

API keys resolved via: env var → `~/.config/ragfer/.env` → `.env` next to binary. No hardcoded URLs or API keys.

### API Authentication (Streamable HTTP mode)

| Env var | Access level |
|---------|-------------|
| `RAG_API_KEY` | Admin — full access (read + write + manage) |
| `RAG_GUEST_API_KEY` | Guest — read-only (query, list, status) |
| (neither set) | Local dev — everything open, no auth |

### Modular LLM profiles

```toml
[[llm_profile]]
name = "fast"
provider = "ollama"
model = "ministral-3:3b"
base_url = "https://api.ollama.com"

[llm]
ingestion_profile = "fast"
query_profile = "smart"
reranker_profile = "fast"
```

Without profiles, all actions use the single `[llm]` provider (backward compatible).

### Tag rules (`tag-rules.toml`)

Tags are **atomic words** (not compound phrases). Filtered with **AND logic**:
- **1 tag** = broad results. Use 1-2 tags max.
- **2 tags** = precise intersection (chunks must have BOTH tags).
- More than 2 tags is overkill — refine the query text instead.

A few compound tags kept as single concepts: `machine learning`, `social media`, `fault tolerance`, `multi agent`.

Pipeline: strip chars → lowercase → synonym lookup → stop word filter → length filter → singular normalization → dedup. Loaded at startup, hot-reloadable via restart.

### Reranker options

- `disabled`: no reranking
- `llm`: uses configured LLM to score results (0-1)
- `cohere`: Cohere Rerank API

## Monitor (TUI)

Built into the binary at `src/monitor/` (3 files: `mod.rs`, `ui.rs`, `api.rs`). Connects to server via HTTP. The TUI exposes `1` Dashboard, `2` Library, `3` Query, `4` Ingest, and `5` Admin. Library supports `j/k` selection and confirmed deletion; Query uses `Q`; Ingest uses `i` and submits through the shared queue. The dashboard remains the live ingestion monitor.

Env vars: `RAGFER_URL`, `RAGFER_KEY`, `RAGFER_REFRESH`.

Keyboard: `TAB` switch panel · `↑↓` scroll · `Enter` open/expand · `c` cycle colors · `C` cancel batch · `x` stop server · `r` rebuild indexes · `f` flush indexes · `l` toggle lists · `s` toggle stats · `g` folder grouping · `o` open in less · `?` help · `q` quit.

Modes: `--demo` (simulate batch), `--fade N` (fade length, default 5).

## Hermes / MCP Client Setup

### stdio (local)

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  rag-ferrite:
    command: /path/to/rag-ferrite
    timeout: 9999
```

API keys resolved via config file chain — no `env` block needed.

### Streamable HTTP (remote/production)

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  rag-ferrite:
    url: "http://localhost:4242/mcp"
    timeout: 9999
```

## Comparison with alternatives

| Feature | rag-ferrite | ClawRAG | mcp-rag-server | RAGent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Binary size | 15 MB | 8 GB+ (Docker) | Node.js | Node.js CLI |
| Language | Rust | Python | TypeScript | TypeScript |
| Database | SQLite | ChromaDB | SQLite | In-memory |
| Hybrid search | BM25 + sqlite-vec + RRF | BM25 + vector + RRF | Vector only | BM25 + vector |
| MCP support | Native | Native | Native | No |
| Relevance scoring | LLM (ingestion) | No | No | No |
| Contextual retrieval | LLM (ingestion) | No | No | No |
| Auto-tagging | LLM (ingestion) | No | No | No |
| Query expansion | LLM (multi-query) | No | No | No |
| Corrective RAG | Auto reformulate | No | No | No |
| LLM reranking | LLM + Cohere | No | No | No |
| Install | `curl \| bash` | Docker Compose | npm install | npm install |
| Dependencies | Zero | Docker, Python, ChromaDB | Node.js | Node.js |
